title: How to complete webslide clip installation on steel stud framing
description: Step-by-step webslide clip installation for steel stud framing: pre-install checklist, on-site stop points, fastener guidance, inspection criteria and Dass.
html:
This step-by-step webslide clip installation guide is written for drywall and framing contractors preparing to fit deflection connectors on steel stud framing. Read the pre-install checklist, follow the numbered steps and stop points, and confirm fastener and model compatibility with the clip manufacturer literature and the Dass Metal product page for local product codes and support Webslide clip.

Pre-install checklist: tools, PPE, fasteners and paperwork

Before you begin webslide clip installation, confirm these items on site. Missing a single tool or the correct datasheet is a common cause of rework.

  • Documents to have: the Dass Metal product page for local product codes and any manufacturer datasheets for the specific WebSlide model called out on your drawings. Keep project framing drawings and the engineer’s notes available.
  • Tools: tape measure, chalk line, level, cordless drill or impact driver with clutch control, calibrated torque driver or torque wrench if required by the datasheet, pliers, and a punch or drift for temporary alignment.
  • PPE: safety glasses, work gloves, hearing protection and steel-toe boots. Follow your site safety plan and local regulations.
  • Fasteners kit: bring the manufacturer-recommended self-drilling or self-tapping screws plus backup fastener types for the stud or track substrate. Do not assume a single fastener will work for every clip and stud gauge; confirm the datasheet.
  • On-site verification: verify stud profiles, track depth and gauge, and confirm the planned clip model is listed for that interface in the manufacturer documentation or with Dass Metal technical support.

Where and when to use WebSlide clips and compatibility notes

WebSlide clips are deflection connectors used where framing must slide to allow differential movement between the structural primary frame and interior steel stud systems. Typical models include WSC 350 and WSC 550, which are common in the deflection connector family for steel framing. Confirm model fit and application using the clip manufacturer literature and Dass Metal product references on the local product page Webslide clip.

Compatibility checks to perform before installation:

  • Confirm clip model against stud flange width and track geometry on the project drawings and the manufacturer tables.
  • Check stud gauge compatibility and whether the clip was designed for light gauge or heavier load bearing systems; refer to the model documentation for recommended pairings.
  • Decide whether a thimble, spacer or shim is specified to maintain the deflection path or to protect fastener heads during movement.

Step-by-step installation with explicit stop points and inspections

Follow these ordered steps on site. Each numbered step ends with a stop point or inspection you must pass before continuing.

1. Layout and measuring

Mark clip locations on the track or structure according to the contract drawings. Use a chalk line for long runs. Stop point: confirm layout marks match the drawings and the correct clip spacing is documented. If spacing differs from the contract, stop and obtain written clarification from the designer or engineer of record.

2. Temporary alignment and mock fit

Temporarily align the stud or track to ensure the clip engages the mating surface without forcing. Insert one clip into position without final fastening and check engagement. Stop point: the clip must slide and seat on the mating web or flange freely. If it binds or requires bending, do not fasten and consult the manufacturer literature or Dass Metal technical support.

3. Clip positioning and engagement

With the stud in the planned location, position the WebSlide clip so its sliding element aligns with the fastener holes provided by the clip. Confirm orientation matches the manufacturer diagram. Stop point: verify the clip orientation and that the design allows the intended vertical or lateral movement. If uncertain, preserve the temporary setup and seek clarification before fastening.

4. Fastener installation sequence

Install the primary fastener or fasteners that locate the clip to the structural member but leave the sliding fastener or fasteners slightly snug to preserve movement. Do not overdrive fasteners. Stop point: after initial fastening, manually slide the clip through its intended range to confirm there is no binding. If movement is impeded, remove the fasteners and recheck alignment.

5. Deflection allowance check and final securement

Confirm the intended deflection gap or range shown on the drawings. Once alignment and free movement are verified, finish-installation fasteners can be set to the torque or seating requirement indicated by the clip manufacturer or the project engineer. Stop point: if the manufacturer requires specific torque values or fastener counts, follow those numbers exactly. If you do not have a torque driver when one is required, stop and obtain the correct tool.

Fastener selection, tools and on-site handling guidance

Exact fastener type, length and head style must follow the clip datasheet and the engineer’s instructions. Typical on-site recommendations are to bring a selection of self-drilling and self-tapping screws sized for the stud thicknesses you will encounter and a torque-controlled driver. Use stainless or zinc-plated fasteners if the project requires corrosion resistance and verify coatings with the specification. Do not invent a universal screw size for WebSlide clips; confirm with the product literature and the Dass product page Webslide clip.

Tools to have on hand:

  • Impact driver with adjustable clutch and correct bits
  • Calibrated torque driver or torque wrench when torque is specified
  • Sheet metal snips and pliers for small adjustments
  • Markers, chalk line and measuring tools

Inspection, acceptance criteria and when to stop work

Use this acceptance checklist before covering any clip installations with drywall:

  • Clip orientation matches the manufacturer diagram and project drawings.
  • All specified fasteners are present and heads are seated without overdrive or stripping.
  • The clip slides freely through the intended movement range without metal-to-metal binding.
  • No deformation, cracks or sharp bends exist in the clip or adjacent stud flange.
  • Required clearances and deflection gaps shown on drawings are verified on site.

Stop work and contact Dass Metal technical support or the structural engineer if:

  • A clip model does not align with the stud or track profile.
  • Fastener heads strip or screw threads pull out of the substrate.
  • The clip cannot achieve its intended sliding motion after initial alignment.

Always refer to the manufacturer documentation for model-specific acceptance criteria. If the project calls for a named clip model, obtain that model’s datasheet and follow the published installation guidance.

Common installer mistakes and how to avoid them

  • Wrong clip orientation: compare to the datasheet diagram before fastening. If you fasten the clip upside down you can eliminate the deflection path.
  • Using incorrect fasteners: do not substitute a shorter or different thread form; verify the screw selection against the datasheet and test one clip first.
  • Overdriving screws: overdriving can clamp the sliding element and prevent movement, so use clutch control or torque tools where required.
  • Assuming cross-brand interchangeability: clips from different manufacturers may look similar but have different engagement geometry. Always check compatibility tables and datasheets.

Safety note: do not confuse WebSlide clips with wire rope clips

WebSlide clips are framing deflection connectors and are unrelated to wire rope clips used in rigging and lifting. Installation methods, torque and safety checks for wire rope clips follow a different standard and must not be applied to framing clips. For a clear example of wire rope clip guidance, consult a dedicated rigging resource so you do not mix product classes wire rope clip guide.

Datasheets, manufacturer literature and printable checklist

Always confirm clip model and installation details in the manufacturer literature. Obtain the relevant WebSlide model datasheet and the local Dass product sheet before you install. For on-site teams, print this article’s pre-install checklist and include the Dass product page and the manufacturer datasheet with project drawings before work begins.

Frequently asked questions

Can I install a WebSlide clip on any steel stud gauge and profile?

No. You must confirm clip-to-stud compatibility with the clip manufacturer’s tables and the Dass Metal product page. Different clip models are designed for specific flange widths and gauges, so consult the relevant model documentation before installation.

How many fasteners do I need per WebSlide clip and what type should I use?

Fastener count and type are specified by the clip datasheet and the project engineer. Carry the recommended fastener types to site and confirm with the manufacturer documentation before fastening. Do not assume a universal screw count; follow the published guidance.

What are the signs a WebSlide clip is incorrectly installed and when should I stop work?

Signs include binding when the clip is manually slid, stripped fastener heads, deformed clip components or misalignment with the stud flange. If any of these occur, stop work and contact Dass Metal technical support or the project structural engineer for direction.

Where can I find the WSC 350 and WSC 550 datasheets, load tables and torque recommendations?

Manufacturer literature for named WebSlide models is available from the clip manufacturer and from Dass Metal. Obtain the model datasheet before installation and follow those specifications for fastener type, thread engagement and torque requirements.

Does Dass Metal supply WebSlide clips and can you ship to U.S. job sites?

Yes. Dass Metal lists WebSlide clips on its product pages and supports cross-border delivery to the United States. Contact Dass Metal via the product page or main site to request a quote and confirm delivery windows Dass Metal Products.

Key takeaway: always verify model, fastener and torque requirements with the clip manufacturer and the project engineer before final installation, and pause work when a fitting or alignment issue appears.
